crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Resection Planning and Margins
children.blurb: Resection planning and margins covers the preoperative and intraoperative work of deciding how much tissue to remove around a tumor or lesion and how to confirm that the removed specimen has an adequate margin.

children.name: Haptic Feedback in Robotic Surgery
children.blurb: Haptic feedback in robotic surgery covers the sensing and display of force, vibration, and texture between a surgical instrument and tissue.

children.name: Virtual Surgical Rehearsal
children.blurb: Virtual surgical rehearsal is the practice of planning and practicing a patient's operation on a digital or physical copy of their anatomy before entering the operating room.

children.name: Tremor Stabilisation in Microsurgery
children.blurb: Tremor stabilisation in microsurgery covers the systems and methods that reduce unintended hand movement during procedures that require precision finer than the human hand can reliably hold.

children.name: Remote Telesurgery
children.blurb: Remote telesurgery is the practice of a surgeon operating on a patient at a different physical location, using a robotic system that translates the surgeon's hand movements into instrument motions at the patient's side.

sections.body: Surgical robotics and navigation covers the machines and software that help a surgeon see, plan and move inside a body. In practice this means imaging pipelines that segment a tumour or organ before the operation, robotic arms that filter hand movement, and consoles that let a surgeon operate through small incisions. Artificial intelligence is doing the unglamorous work here: registering a preoperative scan to the patient on the table, tracking instruments in real time, and predicting where a margin should fall. It is not replacing the surgeon. It is tightening the loop between what was planned and what the tissue actually looks like once the operation starts.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts of this field are settled. Tremor filtering and motion scaling are mature engineering, and robot assisted prostate and gynaecological procedures are routine in many hospitals. Resection planning is partly solved for well imaged tumours and much weaker for tissue that does not show up cleanly on a scan. Haptic feedback remains the honest gap: most clinical systems still give the surgeon little or no true force sensation, so suturing and delicate dissection rely on vision and experience. Telesurgery has been demonstrated across distances but is limited by latency, bandwidth and the question of who is legally responsible when the link fails. Virtual rehearsal is promising and uneven, because it depends on patient specific models that are only as good as the imaging behind them.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages here follow the arc of an operation. Resection Planning and Margins is the starting point, covering how AI segments anatomy and proposes how much to remove. Virtual Surgical Rehearsal takes that plan and lets a surgeon practise the specific case before entering the room. Tremor Stabilisation in Microsurgery sits at the level of the hand, explaining the filtering and scaling that make very small movements possible. Haptic Feedback in Robotic Surgery addresses the sense of touch that most systems still lack, and why that matters for fine work. Remote Telesurgery closes the set by moving the whole arrangement off site, which raises the latency and accountability problems that the earlier pages assume away. Read together they describe one pipeline, from scan to plan to hand to distance.
